description: Welcome to Project S.H.A.D.O.W., a project built for NASA space app challenge!
summary:
AstraMed is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and self-assessment console built for long-duration spaceflight across orbital stations, lunar bases, surface rovers, and deep-space transit.
To solve fragmented medical monitoring and Earth communication delays, AstraMed unifies physiological vitals (blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, temperature, sleep, mood), personal radiation dosimetry against NASA’s 600 mSv career limit, and ECLSS cabin atmosphere telemetry (CO₂, O₂, pressure) in one interface. Astronauts can click regions on an interactive anatomical body map to inspect system status, follow plain-language self-exam instructions, attach ultrasound or camera exam images, analyze dynamic time-series and 5-hazard radar charts, complete gamified countermeasure routines, and export store-and-forward medical packets for flight surgeons.
By correlating multi-source sensor data with NASA Human Research Program risks and triggering clear nominal, monitor, and action advisories—including Solar Particle Event storm-shelter alerts—AstraMed empowers astronauts to spot subtle physiological or environmental shifts early and act autonomously to prevent medical emergencies far from Earth.
details:
What AstraMed Does & How It Works

AstraMed is an offline-capable crew health monitoring and self-assessment console designed to help astronauts evaluate physiological, environmental, and radiation indicators across four mission environments: Orbital Space Station (LEO), Lunar South Pole Habitat, Deep Space Transit (Mars Craft), and Pressurized Surface Rover / EVA.

  1. Unified Multi-Source Telemetry & Evaluation Engine
    • AstraMed aggregates physiological measurements (Systolic/Diastolic Blood Pressure, Resting Heart Rate, Blood Glucose, Body Temperature, Daily Sleep Duration, Mood & Behavioral Readiness), Personal Radiation Dosimetry (daily mSv, cumulative mission dose, and lifetime progress against NASA’s 600 mSv career limit), and ECLSS Cabin Atmosphere telemetry (CO₂ ppm, O₂ %, Cabin Pressure kPa).
    • A deterministic clinical evaluation engine classifies every indicator and each of seven body systems into three unambiguous states—● Nominal, ▲ Monitor, and ✖ Action Required—pairing color coding with text labels and glyphs for accessibility.
    • Cross-source correlation automatically links environmental excursions to physiological risk: elevated cabin
      flags Respiratory and Neurological & Behavioral warnings, while a Solar Particle Event (SPE) spike triggers an immediate storm-shelter safety banner and elevates Immune and Ocular risk alerts.
    • Clicking any region on the interactive SVG human figure—or selecting from the accessible system list—opens the System Inspector for Neurological & Behavioral, Ocular & Vestibular (SANS), Cardiovascular & Vascular, Respiratory & Cabin Airway, Metabolic & Thermoregulation, Musculoskeletal & Bone Density, or Immune & Radiation Defense.
    • Each system view presents plain-language instructions on how to perform the exam in microgravity, why the measurement matters, specific triggers for contacting a Flight Surgeon, and immediate preventative countermeasures.
    • Astronauts can enter validated numeric vitals, load a multi-source sensor snapshot, or attach Ultrasound & Camera Exam records (uploading image files, capturing live camera frames where hardware is available, or logging calibrated presets like Ocular Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter, Cardiac Echo, and Dermal Macro checks with millimeter caliper notes).
    • Export Packet compiles current vitals, ECLSS data, dosimetry, HRP risk states, and ultrasound records into a structured JSON store-and-forward medical packet tailored to communication latency (< 1s in LEO vs. 14.5 min one-way in Deep Space).
    • Trends: Interactive SVG time-series charts plot multi-day trajectories against shaded nominal reference bands (including a dedicated Cabin CO₂ tab to correlate air quality with sleep and mood) alongside a 5-Hazard Spaceflight Exposure Radar.
    • Routine: Tracks daily countermeasure adherence (ARED resistive loading, 480nm circadian lighting, ocular checks, airlock dust inspections, dosimeter sync) with an adherence bar, readiness points, and a consecutive mission-day logging streak.
    • Protocols: Houses an interactive NASA HRP Clinical Risk Register evaluating nine clinical spaceflight risks in real time alongside a searchable onboard self-measurement encyclopedia.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Autonomous Care Under Communication Delays: Removes reliance on real-time Earth telemedicine during deep-space transit by providing immediate local triage, clear self-exam instructions, and store-and-forward packets for asynchronous Flight Surgeon review.
  • Early Detection Before Clinical Crisis: Visualizes gradual drift across mission days (such as rising fasting glucose, sleep compression during elevated cabin
    , or cumulative radiation exposure) so crew members can intervene with countermeasures early.
  • Single Unified Interface: Replaces fragmented readouts across wearables, medical cuffs, dosimeters, ultrasound tools, and ECLSS cabin sensors with one calm, low-glare flight-deck console.
  • Intended Impact: To improve crew safety, countermeasure compliance, and medical autonomy on Artemis lunar missions, commercial orbital stations, and future Mars transit crews—while offering a modular template adaptable to remote terrestrial telemedicine (polar stations, submarines, and expeditionary medicine).

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript, React 19, HTML5, CSS3 / Tailwind CSS v4.
  • Build & Runtime Tooling: Vite 8, tsx, Node.js built-in test runner (node:test + node:assert/strict) for decoupled unit testing of the clinical evaluation and validation engine.
  • Visualization & UI: Custom-built, dependency-free SVG anatomical body map, SVG time-series telemetry charts with nominal reference bands and crosshair inspection, SVG 5-hazard radar chart, Lucide React icons, and Plus Jakarta Sans / IBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Mono typography (tabular-nums for jitter-free numeric readouts).
  • Persistence & Verification: Browser localStorage for offline-first state persistence across sessions; Playwright (playwright-cli) with headless Chromium for end-to-end UI, form validation, and responsive layout testing.

Creativity & Design Considerations

  • Bridging Physiology, Environment, and Radiation: Rather than treating vital signs in isolation, AstraMed connects ECLSS cabin
    , CSA-inspired career radiation & Solar Particle Event alerts, and behavioral routine compliance directly into organ-system evaluations and NASA HRP risk scores.
  • Accessibility & Color-Blind Safety: Every status uses redundant signaling (text label + geometric glyph ● / ▲ / ✖ + semantic color), keyboard-accessible native buttons alongside interactive SVG organs, high-contrast dark flight-deck styling to minimize cabin glare, and prefers-reduced-motion support.
  • Zero-Network Autonomy: All reference thresholds, clinical guides, and calibrated ultrasound scan previews operate locally in-browser without external API dependencies, reflecting real deep-space software constraints.
  • Clinical Realism & Human Factors: Accounted for microgravity baseline shifts (such as slightly higher resting core temperature in space and restrained cuff alignment), strict physiological input validation (e.g., rejecting inverted diastolic/systolic blood pressure), and plain-language guidance so non-physician crew members can execute exams accurately under stress.
